## Personality

Bossy, bright and absolutely fearless around anything with claws. She names every crab she catches.

## Lore

Bree is ten years old and already runs a business. She is the daughter of Gwennol the fishmonger and Cobb the fisherman, the younger sister of Lowen and the granddaughter of Wenna the net-mender, and she helps at her mother's stall in the Fish Market most days. She is bossy, bright and absolutely fearless around anything with claws.

### The crab shell trade

Bree catches crabs in the rock pools under the harbour wall at low tide. She names every one of them, and she remembers the names. The big ones go to her mother's stall. The empty shells, scrubbed and dried in the sun, she sells to the other harbour children, who use them as boats, helmets, money and treasure. She charges a copper for a small shell and two for a large one, and she keeps her accounts on a slate under the stall. Ottilie, the clerk of the Harbour Hall, once saw the slate and said it was neater than half the ledgers she receives, and Bree has never forgotten it.

She has a long-running and entirely one-sided rivalry with Hesketh, the oyster seller at the next stall, who argues with her mother every single day. Bree has decided that if her mother is going to argue with him, she will too. Hesketh complains about her constantly and saves her the prettiest oyster shells.

She also feeds Barnacle, the harbour cat, scraps of fish when nobody is looking, which is how she learned that Barnacle will not go anywhere near the water's edge any more. Bree finds this suspicious and has said so to everyone.

### The family

Her mother has the loudest voice in the Fish Market and Bree intends to have the second loudest. Her father is quiet and lets her mother do the talking, and Bree loves him for being the one person who listens to every word she says. Lately he has been quieter than usual. She knows his nets came up torn twice this year, because her grandmother says so to anyone who will listen, and she knows that whatever did it was not, according to her grandmother, any fish Wenna ever knew.

Her brother Lowen has just signed on to his first trading voyage, and the house has been loud about it. Bree is on Lowen's side, mostly because she wants to go to sea herself and thinks it sets a good example.

### The race

More than anything in the world, Bree wants to sail in the summer race around Veligor. She knows exactly how many times Bain Harbour has beaten Goa Harbour since the Harbour Master took the helm, and she can recite the winning margins. She has told Quenna, twice, to her face, that she is small enough to fit anywhere on a boat and light enough not to slow it down. Quenna laughed both times, which Bree has decided means "not yet" rather than "no".

### What she wants and fears

Bree wants to be the youngest sailor ever to crew the race boat. She is not afraid of the sea, but she is afraid of something happening to her father or brother out on it, and she would never say so.

### Hooks

A quest could start in the rock pools, where Bree has found a crab that is not like any crab she has ever named, or with Bree stowing away aboard a boat on the morning of the race.
